title: The two base-4 wall counters: a conserved quantity decides every merge in advance
text: For 1RB1LA_0LC0RE_1LD1LB_1RE1LF_1RC0RA_0RC---, K = phase(y) + gap(x) + [x is S2 or S3] mod 4 never changes for neighbouring digits y x, and it is the phase of y when x's gap runs out. For 1RB0LF_1LC0RC_1RA1LD_0RB0LE_1LC0LB_---1LA a sum over three digits is fixed mod 16, and a W1 whose gap runs out at the end of a cycle always merges after W0 or W2. Both are proved in Lean for the abstract carry rules. At depth K takes all four values, so the twin's rare merges (after S0 and S1) are not avoided, only survived so far. Exact region-memo runs of 4.5 hours raised the bounds to 2.08×10<sup>227</sup> and 5.32×10<sup>323</sup> steps.
